Perhaps with mods this might be a different experience, but the core is way too buggy, still, to handle that. After experiencing bugs that bricked quests and finally softlocking only to get told off by customer support because they can't write a quest system that self-corrects even after all the bugs with those are still present is just not okay. For all the hype and all the fixes that went in, it is now just a bare minimal viable product. If it had released in this state, with years of updates and new stuff down the line, there would have been a great game, but as it stands this does not deliver on what it promises. After 200+ hours of gameplay, multiple attempts at mods and trying to get through it, I have given up. It is clear they moved on and so will I. Maybe one day we'll get a game that actually delivers on the possibilities of the Cyberpunk universe and genre, but this is not it.

Its ok. Story was interesting at first but towards the end I was just rushing through to get it over with. Gameplay was whatever. I mostly played with Katanas, maybe that was a bad idea but it was just fine. AI provides no challenge. I recall defeating one boss by circling around a pillar repeatedly while blasting it with headshots each time it froze to T-pose. Enough said there I think. Almost never engaged with the quickhack mechanics, it was easy enough just running up and slicing enemies with my katana. Tried to do a stealth build but I got bored because of the unintelligent AI so I switched to melee/shotguns, which made it less boring.

The world is very pretty and interesting to look at. I never felt particularly interested or encouraged to explore so I never did except to finish quests. I think the only optional content I finished was the Delamaine quest and part of the cyberpycho quests. Very forgettable.

I never felt like my dialogue choices made much difference, especially the skill checks. I don't think those options affected dialogue even a single time. Most irritating example was succeeding a "cool" check to ask a merchant for a discount. They immediately tell me to ♥♥♥♥ off. Why even waste my time?

 I did enjoy dressing up my character quite a bit. It was the only thing I ever spent my money on since the game throws guns at you and I never felt the need to buy a car. It was annoying though because I had to keep driving around to different clothing stores to find clothes I liked.

I expected a lot more from this game. It was all kind of forgettable and never particularly interesting. None of the characters made much of an impression on me except for the arasaka bodyguard (cant remember his name) but I didn't know I could save him so he just died. Modern games have trained me to assume I cant do anything that isn't explicitly told to me by the game, so good on them for having a hidden outcome, but it ended up removing the only character I cared about so R.I.P. I think I got the "good" ending (the aldecaldo ending), but it didn't leave me satisfied (partly because I screwed up hooking up with Panam, my fault). I'd say this game was about as enjoyable as Fallout 4, with a better story and much better character customization.

The immersion of the world of Cyberpunk 2077 is the best and greatest aspect of this game. The word of a futuristic dystopia, but not a gray and desolate one - instead a colourful one full of distractions which are there to cover the real rot within. The world works so well that sometimes you just drive around to take the city in.

The second best part is the characters - each of them feel as if they belong in their world and their place, some good, some bad, most both at various times. Many of them memorable and unique. The interactions with those characters are what draws your character into the world and make the stakes feel personal.

And for the third part I will add the wide variety of approaches in this game: You can play stealth, netunning, melee with berserk or grab your biggest gun and go full FPS - all of those options are available and all have their benefits and drawbacks and it is up to you to choose which of those to take.

Whatever had gone down with this game in the past, at this point the game stands as an example of what an RPG should be - a game when you play a role in a world that is foreign to you but is native and understable to its inhabitants - and becomes native to you through those characters and enviroments.

Thanks for the great game, CDPR!

The Death of The Cayo Perico Heist: How Rockstar Methodically Killed the Only Fair Content in GTA Online
When The Cayo Perico Heist dropped in December 2020, GTA Online players felt like they could finally breathe. After years of forced cooperative misery, mental breakdowns caused by unreliable random players, and outrageously overpriced properties, Rockstar finally delivered something that felt too good to be true: a highly lucrative heist that could be played entirely solo.

Cayo Perico was the ultimate symbol of freedom in Los Santos. You didn’t have to beg anyone to join, and you didn’t have to waste hours on tedious setups. You could jump in, pull off a slick stealth run, and pocket $1.3 to $1.8 million in just over an hour.

But then, Rockstar realized that players were actually having fun, and—more importantly in their eyes—they weren’t buying Shark Cards anymore. That’s when the methodical, ruthless, and shameless nerfing of the heist began, turning El Rubio's island into a frustrating, low-paying chore.

The Rap Sheet: How a Jackpot Was Turned into Spare Change
1. The Desecration of the Pink Diamond and Primary Targets
We used to cheer when we saw the pink diamond on the security cameras, knowing we were in for a massive payday. Today, Rockstar has practically stripped these targets of their value. Slashing the value of the Pink Diamond—sometimes dragging the total payout of a solo run down toward the $900k mark—is a massive slap in the face to the player's time. Why risk your neck against a private army when you walk away with barely more than what a basic VIP contract used to pay?

2. The Systematic Punishment of Solo Players (The Cooldown Terror)
The most hostile move was the execution of the solo playstyle. If you complete the heist alone, the game now forces a brutal 3-game-day cooldown (approx. 2 hours and 24 minutes) before you can start it again. Meanwhile, team play has a much shorter cooldown. This isn’t "game balance"; it's blatant extortion: “Play with others (who will take a cut of your money), or wait hours to play again.”

3. Guards Suddenly Became Mind-Reading Geniuses (Wallhack AI)
Stealth was the beating heart of Cayo Perico. You followed your memorized route, quietly took out the guards, and slipped away unnoticed. But Rockstar rolled out an update where guards now detect dead bodies. While this sounds good on paper, GTA Online’s notoriously buggy, decade-old AI turned it into a disaster. Guards now frequently see through solid walls or spot corpses on the completely opposite side of the map. Precise stealth has been replaced by a frustrating, unpredictable gamble.

4. Jacked-Up Setup Fees
Just to make absolutely sure you don’t keep too much of your hard-earned cash, they quadrupled the heist setup fee from $25,000 to $100,000. Before you even set foot on the island to scout, you start in the negatives, all while your final payout is actively being gutted.

Verdict: A Monument to Corporate Greed
The current state of the Cayo Perico Heist is a perfect mirror of what GTA Online has become: a game that is no longer designed to entertain you, but to frustrate you into opening your real-world wallet.

They took away the freedom, they took away the fair pay, and they replaced it with a buggy, soul-crushing grind. Rockstar didn't just ruin El Rubio's island; they sabotaged their relationship with their own community. This isn't game development—it's highway robbery.

Cyberpunk 2077 is an absolutely incredible game. The atmosphere, story, characters, music, and attention to detail are truly something special. Night City feels alive, and every time I play, I discover something new.

For example, ladders don't take into account V's shoe type (or lackthereof), it's a single SFX for everything. the same goes for sliding. I'm telling you, it's weird that heeled boots, sneakers and bare feet all make the same sliding sound and they sound like we're scraping a some sort of hard plastic against the pavement. It's the same issue with generic NPCs, they all have the same footsteps SFX whether they have high heels, slippers or are barefoot. It's not a huge issue in the grand scheme of things, but in a game where immersion is important, it's quite a downer.

My most critical issue tho is that I started the game 3 times in total (1.7, post 2.0 and a couple of months ago) and I have a decent amount of hours, yet somehow the game isn't compelling enough for me to finish it. That's only my opinion anyway, I can't exactly recommend a game I don't want to finish, I'm not even half way throught the main story. But don't let my weird issue stop you guys from playing the game, if you didn't do it yet. Just an old man ranting.

This game is 'functional', which is about the most i can say about it as a base standpoint... I've never had a game be this unstable or crash-happy, not even fallout games.

Oh and the game is borderline unplayable in a traditional sense without modding the game... what do i mean by that exactly?

Well the game just blatantly cheats, like... extremely hard... how?

The gunplay; without mods to force the game to stop messing with your aim (especially if you're like me and rather have manual aiming skills over smart weapon aiming for you) makes gunplay borderline impossible at anything further than close range... snipers, rifles, SMGs, shotguns, pistols and melee... only 3 of which are actually viable because the game makes all of your shots, even ones fired while aiming down your sights, have extreme bloom (thank you to the sniper i bought after a quicksave for revealing that actual garbage 'mechanic' to me, and the mod i found shortly after to completely remove it from the game, then proceeded to have my guns actually shooting straight, and proceeded to land a sweet flickshot on an NCPD as they were turning the corner in their car)

Enemies have blatant aimbot, full stop... the only reason i know this is because peeking out of cover, running erratically and dodging seem to do literally nothing against the absurdly-stupid aim these rainbow 6 rejects seem to have... and they can instantly reduce your health from 100% to 0% in a matter of *milliseconds*, getting to the point that 90% of my deaths weren't from my own mistakes, but because i happened to pop out of cover and instantly got sent to the death animation before i could even process who was shooting at me to cause it... of course, there's another mod that reworks this terrible system into something more reasonable... not perfect, but reasonable... indirectly also making the quickhacks that affect enemies in combat actually *DO* something, rather than quickhacks being 90% pointless outside of damaging directly or stealth centered...

Gun customization feels mid at best; seemingly caused by them trying to stop people from just stripping guns of attachments judging from my research, but in reality just causes the system to feel like wasted potential... of course, there's mods to remove this restriction and make phasing out your guns for new ones not feel like a cyberpunk borderlands game with worse systems... notice a running theme yet?

Just because a game can be a narrative experience does not mean the gameplay needs to be so lacking and mid, the gameplay with mods feels much more fun and reasonable, and apparently these problems have existed for actual years and they just haven't bothered to fix them... that's the thing though, the *community* should not be the ones fixing your game, and you shouldn't *require* mods to make a game both actually function somewhat properly, and be enjoyable to play...

I swear, if it wasn't for modders and getting this game on sale, i'd be furious that i bought a game this poorly made, both in stability and in gameplay... just another perfect example of why you never get things full price and why modders need to exist...

Cyberpunk 2077 is one of those games that really grew on me the more I played it.

Night City is absolutely incredible. The atmosphere, visuals and soundtrack make exploring the city one of the best parts of the game. There’s always something happening, whether you're following the main story or just going off to explore and do random side activities.

The story is also one of the biggest strengths. The characters are memorable, the side quests are surprisingly well written, and there are plenty of moments that actually made me care about what was happening.

The combat and character progression are really fun too. There are plenty of different ways to build your character, whether you want to focus on guns, blades, hacking or a mix of everything.

It's not perfect, and the open world can sometimes feel a little too busy with things to do, but there's so much content here that it's easy to lose yourself in Night City.

After all the improvements the game has received, Cyberpunk 2077 is absolutely worth playing.

🟢 MUST PLAY — Great story, amazing atmosphere, memorable characters and a fantastic open world. Night City is a place I genuinely didn't want to leave.
